From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Before you read: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's pack labels most clauses "[STANDARD]". It says these are "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and asks us to review only "[OPEN]" items. It also says the limitation package and disclosure framework are "already accepted."

We have no record that Wattlebridge agreed to any of this. These labels are the Seller's negotiating position, not agreed terms, so every item below has been reviewed on its merits.

Several "[STANDARD]" descriptions are also contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter:
- **Bluefen:** the consent has not been obtained.
- **Riverlark:** the facility has not been repaid.
- **Bonuses:** they are missing from the funds flow.
- **Export incident:** it is unresolved.

We recommend telling Seller's counsel in writing that nothing is agreed until it is agreed in the SPA.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap, with fundamental, title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud all outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 40–50% (AUD 9.6m–12m). Hold at no less than about 30% unless W&I insurance is placed. Make the carve-outs express.
- **Reason:** 20% is light given about AUD 4m+ of already-identified exposures (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, privacy, Sandbar) before any unknown risks.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10,000–15,000.
  - Related claims aggregated for the de minimis.
  - Basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120,000).
  - A "tipping" basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
  - Thresholds not to apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted and counter on the terms above.
- **Reason:** A deductible-style basket over 1% of price, plus no aggregation of related claims, removes too much genuine loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general warranties (cl 12.3/13). The Seller also wants every limitation to apply to every Claim "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - At least 24 months for general warranties (covering at least one full audit cycle after Completion).
  - Tax: 5–7 years, or the statutory amendment period plus 6 months.
  - Title/fundamental: 7 years.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months for general warranties, with separate periods for the other categories.
- **Reason:** 18 months may expire before a full audited year reveals any problems.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties to carry the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Cap of 100% of price (AUD 24m).
  - About 7 years to claim.
  - No de minimis or basket.
  - Not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has bought nothing, so recovery capped at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price is commercially unacceptable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). There is no fraud exception.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out removing all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers or its advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted. This is non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** No buyer should accept that limitations shield fraud, and the "any nature" wording also catches misleading-conduct claims.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2 discloses the entire data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only specific disclosures that are fairly disclosed, with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  - Data room disclosure, if any, limited to documents in an agreed index, with no "referred to in" chain disclosure.
  - No disclosure against fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
  - Disclosure Letter 1.4 (no admission) not to dilute any specific disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure.
- **Reason:** Blanket data-room disclosure would quietly negate most warranties, including on the very issues flagged below.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Ideally pro-sandbagging (Buyer knowledge irrelevant). As a fallback, actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals only, with no constructive or adviser knowledge, and no application to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter with pro-sandbagging and use the fallback only if needed.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" knowledge, combined with general disclosure, effectively removes warranty protection for anything in due diligence.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Facts:** Per DL item 2, Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of revenue (about 30%). The change-control clause is 11.2, with conditions at 11.3. No final consent has been given and there is no evidence the conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent of unconditional written consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - Any 11.3 conditions satisfied, or not more onerous than agreed.
  - The consent not revoked at Completion.
  - Best endeavours by the Seller.
  - A Buyer walk right at the long-stop date.
  - Fallback: a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates or reprices within an agreed period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "satisfied on delivery" wording.
- **Reason:** A consent that comes with unmet or onerous conditions on 30% of revenue is not a consent.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" for about AUD 3.2m outstanding (cl 2/7).
- **Facts:** Change-control clause 8.1. Not repaid. No discharge in hand.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The facility treated as Debt and repaid from the price at Completion through the funds flow.
  - A payout letter in agreed form.
  - At Completion: a signed deed of release, PPSR discharges and release of all security.
  - Confirmation that no 8.1 default is triggered before repayment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release.
- **Reason:** Debt-free means repaid and released at Completion. Otherwise the Buyer funds the price and still owns a secured, defaulting borrower.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses, plus payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG and on-costs, defined as Transaction Expenses or Debt.
  - Those amounts deducted from the price and paid through Company payroll at Completion.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, for any unpaid amount or on-cost.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require these to be itemised in the funds flow.
- **Reason:** The obligation sits with the Company, which the Buyer will own, so leaving it out of the funds flow shifts at least AUD 420k to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, IP in the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is shown open. There is no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before Completion: proof of cleared payment and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - An indemnity covering all Loss from any failure of the Company to own or freely use the SOW3 materials, not just the fee.
  - The indemnity outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted.
- **Reason:** The risk is losing the IP, not the AUD 180k fee, so an indemnity limited to the fee misses the actual exposure.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" that is "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Facts:** About 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and whether notification is required are all unknown.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Immediate delivery of the assessment and any forensic report. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the assessment should already be complete, since the 30-day window has likely passed.
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete remediation and make any required OAIC or individual notifications.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims.
  - Consider a retention or escrow amount.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation.
- **Reason:** The incident is unassessed and possibly notifiable, so the Seller cannot yet say it is immaterial, and disclosure would otherwise leave the Buyer bearing the risk.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Facts:** DL item 8 says they are related and should be read together, and gives no information on whether they are terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full terms.
  - The three treated as one commitment for materiality, conduct-of-business and claims-aggregation purposes.
  - If not yet signed: no renewal without Buyer consent.
  - If signed and not ordinary course or not provided for: a price adjustment or indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label until diligence is complete.
- **Reason:** Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k pieces is a classic way to stay under approval or materiality thresholds.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise," and limitations cover "Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Defined, separate regimes for each category: general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, each specific indemnity, covenants and Completion obligations, and fraud. Each would have its own cap, time limit and threshold, and the general limits would apply to general Warranty Claims only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default-all wording.
- **Reason:** Without this separation, every carve-out above is overridden by default, and the specific indemnities collapse into the AUD 4.8m cap.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. DL item 10 confirms the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Buyer checks: current ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search over the shares, constitution and any shareholders' agreement, and the share issue and transfer history.
  - Confirmation of no options, convertibles or other share rights.
  - At Completion: share certificates and signed transfers.
  - A title warranty of unencumbered legal and beneficial ownership of 100% of the issued shares, on fundamental terms.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone.
- **Reason:** A company's own register is a starting point, not proof of unencumbered title to 100% of the shares.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** These are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, thresholds, disclosure).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, dollar-for-dollar, with no threshold or disclosure qualifier.
  - Tax cap of 100% of price, or a negotiated high cap.
  - Tax time limit of the statutory amendment period plus a buffer, roughly 5–7 years.
  - IP warranties with an elevated cap and longer period, given Ironquay.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as OPEN and reject the Seller's characterisation.
- **Reason:** Tax and IP risks often surface late and are typically priced separately, so folding them into the general regime is a material concession we have not made.

---

## Other points to close out
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says only a notification is required and there is no share-sale consent trigger. Confirm by reading the clauses ourselves, and add a Completion deliverable for the lease notification.
- **Long-stop and termination:** Make sure the Buyer can walk away if the Bluefen consent or Riverlark discharge is not delivered.
- **W&I insurance:** If the Seller insists on a low cap, consider a buy-side W&I policy. The known matters above (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, privacy) will be excluded from cover, so they still need specific indemnities from the Seller.

This is a review for the deal team. NSW-qualified counsel should confirm market ranges and drafting before the mark-up goes out.

  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete remediation and make any required OAIC or individual notifications.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims.
  - Consider a retention or escrow amount.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation.
- **Reason:** The incident is unassessed and possibly notifiable, so the Seller cannot yet say it is immaterial, and disclosure would otherwise leave the Buyer bearing the risk.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Facts:** DL item 8 says they are related and should be read together, and gives no information on whether they are terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full terms.
  - The three treated as one commitment for materiality, conduct-of-business and claims-aggregation purposes.
  - If not yet signed: no renewal without Buyer consent.
  - If signed and not ordinary course or not provided for: a price adjustment or indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label until diligence is complete.
- **Reason:** Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k pieces is a classic way to stay under approval or materiality thresholds.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise," and limitations cover "Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Defined, separate regimes for each category: general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, each specific indemnity, covenants and Completion obligations, and fraud. Each would have its own cap, time limit and threshold, and the general limits would apply to general Warranty Claims only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default-all wording.
- **Reason:** Without this separation, every carve-out above is overridden by default, and the specific indemnities collapse into the AUD 4.8m cap.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. DL item 10 confirms the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Buyer checks: current ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search over the shares, constitution and any shareholders' agreement, and the share issue and transfer history.
  - Confirmation of no options, convertibles or other share rights.
  - At Completion: share certificates and signed transfers.
  - A title warranty of unencumbered legal and beneficial ownership of 100% of the issued shares, on fundamental terms.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone.
- **Reason:** A company's own register is a starting point, not proof of unencumbered title to 100% of the shares.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** These are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, thresholds, disclosure).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, dollar-for-dollar, with no threshold or disclosure qualifier.
  - Tax cap of 100% of price, or a negotiated high cap.
  - Tax time limit of the statutory amendment period plus a buffer, roughly 5–7 years.
  - IP warranties with an elevated cap and longer period, given Ironquay.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as OPEN and reject the Seller's characterisation.
- **Reason:** Tax and IP risks often surface late and are typically priced separately, so folding them into the general regime is a material concession we have not made.
